source_excerpt: Atlas and Boreal were run on the same 100 fixed queries. Query order was randomized independently for each system. Table 1 reports exact-match counts and arithmetic mean end-to-end latency; no query was excluded. Higher exact match and lower latency are better.
source_table: System | correct/100 | exact match | mean latency; Atlas | 82 | 82% | 120 ms; Boreal | 82 | 82% | 150 ms
experimental_setup: Both systems used dataset D-fixed split T1; the same retrieved passages; generator G-7; prompt P-3; deterministic decoding; one X90 GPU; batch size 1; and 10 warm-up requests followed by the same 100 timed requests.
audited_claim: Under the documented single-GPU, batch-size-1 setup, Atlas matched Boreal's exact-match accuracy and reduced mean latency by 20%.
source_locator: Instructor dossier S01, Methods paragraph and Table 1

source_excerpt: The dossier reports one poisoning run. In that run, the attacker read target queries, inserted passages into the corpus, selected insertions after inspecting retriever outputs, and could insert at most 20 passages per query. The dossier contains no results from another poisoning run. Lower attack success is better. Table 2 also reports clean exact match.
source_table: Defense | successful attacks/200 | attack success | clean exact match; Shield | 18/200 | 9% | 80%; Guard | 50/200 | 25% | 80%
experimental_setup: Shield and Guard used the same 200 target queries, corpus snapshot, retriever R-2, generator G-4, prompt, poisoning script, insertion limit, and scoring rule.
audited_claim: Across retrieval-poisoning attacks, Shield is more effective than Guard.
source_locator: Instructor dossier S02, Methods paragraph and Table 2
